title: Être vs. Avoir
explanation: 'Être' (to be) and 'avoir' (to have) are the two core auxiliary verbs in French and are used to form other tenses like the passé composé.

title: Gender of Nouns: le / la
explanation: Every French noun is masculine (le) or feminine (la), and this isn't always predictable from the word's meaning, so it's usually memorized with the noun.

title: Present Tense -er Verbs
explanation: The largest group of French verbs ends in -er. Drop -er and add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent.

examples.text: parler -> je parle, tu parles, il parle
nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent

title: Question Formation with Est-ce que
explanation: Adding 'est-ce que' before a statement turns it into a question without changing word order - the simplest way to ask questions in French.

examples.text: Est-ce que tu aimes le café ?
